newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Zagrebacka Banka cuts interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Zagrebacka Banka cuts interest rates.

text.p: Leading Croatian commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka d.d. said on Friday it would cut interest rates on kuna loans and deposits from September 1.
It said in a press release the lending rate for companies would be cut by two percentage points. The rate is currently 23 percent, except for prime borrowers.
The citizens' giro and current account credit rate would go down to 18 percent from 20 percent.
"This is a first step to be followed, if the market conditions remain stable, by a further lowering of rates on kuna credits," the bank said.
Parallel with the lending rate cut, Zagrebacka also decided to bring down by one percentage point the interest paid on all term deposits in the domestic currency.
They now range between 2.50 and 10.50 percent.
However, to stimulate longer-term savings in foreign exchange, the bank will raise by one point the current rate for deposits exceeding one year.

Since June, the minimum 12-month rate has been 3.07 percent for deposits of up to 8,200 Swiss francs and the maximum 7.09 percent for dollar deposits running up to $201,000. The interest on higher amounts is negotiable. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
